args.summary: Woman in her 60s with 1 week of dyspnea and a new dry cough. She needs 4 L/min nasal O2 to keep saturation above 92%. Exam: reduced breath sounds at the left base and diffuse fine crackles; no lymphadenopathy or organomegaly. History: rheumatoid arthritis with stable CTD-ILD for 5 years, asbestos exposure, and immunosuppression with baricitinib and methotrexate. Contrast CT chest: moderate left effusion with nodular circumferential pleural thickening that includes the mediastinal pleura. These pleural findings strongly suggest malignant pleural disease, most likely mesothelioma. Next step is a tissue and fluid diagnosis.
working_diagnoses: Malignant pleural mesothelioma (asbestos exposure; nodular circumferential and mediastinal pleural thickening)
Metastatic pleural malignancy (e.g., adenocarcinoma or lymphoma; JAK inhibitor/methotrexate-associated lymphoproliferative disorder)
Infectious pleural effusion or empyema, including tuberculous pleuritis, in an immunosuppressed host
Methotrexate pneumonitis or acute exacerbation of CTD-ILD
next_actions: Ultrasound-guided diagnostic and therapeutic left thoracentesis: pleural fluid protein, LDH, glucose, pH, cell count and differential, cytology, Gram stain and culture, AFB and ADA
Serum CBC, CMP, LDH, and CRP
If cytology is nondiagnostic, arrange CT- or thoracoscopy-guided pleural biopsy with immunohistochemistry
Continue oxygen and hold methotrexate and baricitinib while the workup is in progress

args.rationale: Woman in her 60s with ongoing low oxygen, needing 4 L/min by nasal cannula to keep saturation above 92% (physical_exam_004). She has a moderate left effusion with nodular thickening all around the pleura, including the mediastinal pleura (imaging_008). Fluid from a high-volume thoracentesis showed atypical epithelioid and spindle cells positive for SOX10, Melan-A and S100 and negative for calretinin, EMA, p40 and WT1 (procedure_result_009). This fits pleural melanoma with a malignant effusion, primary site unknown; the skin and eye exams found no primary (physical_exam_011). She also has rheumatoid arthritis with CTD-ILD (pmh_002) and takes baricitinib plus methotrexate (meds_003). Because of the oxygen need, the new cancer and her immunosuppression, she needs inpatient care, not discharge. ICU is not needed now because her other vital signs are normal.
args.followup_or_handoff: Admit to an internal medicine or pulmonary ward with oncology consulted. Continue oxygen with a target saturation of 92-96% and watch for the effusion re-accumulating. Arrange repeat bedside ultrasound, and involve interventional pulmonology early for a definitive plan: an indwelling pleural catheter or thoracoscopy with biopsy and pleurodesis. Send the cell block for confirmatory pathology and molecular testing (BRAF V600, NRAS, KIT). Stage with whole-body PET-CT or CT of chest, abdomen and pelvis plus MRI of the brain. Look for a primary with a full dermatology exam including the scalp, nails and mucosa, a dilated eye exam, and a gynecologic/anorectal and ENT mucosal assessment. Get CBC, CMP, LDH and CRP. With rheumatology, hold baricitinib and methotrexate; this matters for both infection risk and any future immunotherapy. Consider PJP and TB screening before systemic therapy, and review her CTD-ILD before immune checkpoint inhibitors because of pneumonitis risk. Refer to the multidisciplinary melanoma tumor board, and start goals-of-care discussions and a palliative care referral early.
